subtype: Approach: leaving the whole plan to the adults [Pitfall]
passage: Note from Charu, Kiran's mother. Two weeks before the holiday I asked Kiran what he would like to see. He shrugged, kept playing his game and said, "You decide." So the rest of us made the plan. On the second day, at the old stepwell, Kiran sat on a step and said it was boring; he wanted the model railway museum. It had never been on the list because he had never told us. He cried on the way to the next place, angry with us and, I think, a little with himself. That evening I asked him for one wish for the last day, and we changed the plan together. - Charu

qa.q: Where was Kiran when he said the day was boring?
qa.a: He was sitting on a step at the old stepwell.

qa.q: What was Kiran feeling on the way to the next place?
qa.a: Angry and upset, with the family and perhaps a little with himself.

qa.q: What could Kiran have done before the trip, and why?
qa.a: Kiran could have named one thing he wanted to see, so it could be included in the plan from the start.

qa.q: How does Charu see what went wrong on the trip?
qa.a: Charu notices that Kiran's wishes were missing rather than that the plan was bad, so she invites him to add one for the last day.

grounding: A child leaves the trip plan to adults, and is upset when the places do not match his interests.
